hypothesis: For a cross-session question, shifting skill probability when the earliest supporting fact arrives can have more delayed influence than shifting the same pair at the final evidence-bearing session. Use labelled evidence only to select and compare experimental interventions. A deployable policy sees only its current ordinary state, never the question or future evidence. This local intervention study is not a claim about a full deployed policy.
panel: Use the entire previously registered full-prefix training panel: 185 unique questions, 99 final endpoints, 165 (history, earliest evidence session, final session) groups, six training histories. Keep multiple questions at the same intervention together. Hold the existing reproducible fair background fixed, including the final background action determined by the original hash. Existing last-pivot trajectories supply the factual background outcome and the alternative last action. Measure the one missing trajectory per group by toggling only the first evidence-bearing span, retaining all intervening sessions and the exact ordered skills previously executed at every other position. Compare the three distinct measured trajectories. Reuse only exact greedy physical response-cache hits. Registration must precede new switched-branch scores. Service gives other jobs a turn between trajectories; no additional unbounded GPU instance.
policy: Use solely the frozen joint-mask rank-allocation model, selected before this trial; keep the jointly checked labels, held-history rules and native rates. Use root rules for session 1, terminal rules for states with earlier memory. Numerical forecasts for earliest and final positions are bound to the unperturbed actual pre-write states before scoring the new trajectory. Keep controls for return-only rank, within-history permuted credit, soft kernel, native and terminal PPO. Compare measured expected F1 at each location under its own local native probability with the same remaining background actions. Compare differences relative to the common physical background separately from differences relative to native. Never replace an unknown outcome with a predicted F1.
checks: Verify identity of the checkpoint skill versions, source text, all pre-pivot decisions and bank changes, pre-pivot retrieval and references, K=3 and the two common slots; after the pivot the retrieved memories may differ but every ordered skill must be identical to the corresponding factual one. Recompute reader F1 with the original corpus answers, verify local-to-original QA indices, stable memory-version origins, model calls and tokens. Record both returned answers for strict-recovery candidates. A strict flip is only a candidate for later same-skill execution and retrieval repairs. No new extra selection credit is granted by this measurement alone.
timing: Report all matched questions, the subset where neither last-action control had a score at study registration, and whether the new earlier counterfactual had a score before each numeric forecast. Keep early/late contrasts, per-type and per-history values and clustered intervals. Prefix lengths and evidence gaps are reported. These six training histories only inform the next independent development decision. Locked full LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S remain necessary for generalization.
